title: The Best Way to Clean a Glass Stovetop Without Scratching
hook: A glass stovetop looks beautiful until it's covered in burnt-on spills and cloudy streaks. And one wrong scrub can leave scratches forever. Here are seven safe steps to bring your glass cooktop back to a mirror shine without damaging it. No special skills are needed, just patience.
intro: Glass-ceramic cooktops are tougher than they look, but they can scratch. The golden rule is simple: soften first, and scrape only when you must. Heat bakes spills onto the glass, so the cleaning is about loosening them with a gentle product and some time, then lifting them off. We'll use baking soda, a little vinegar, a cooktop cleaner, and a razor scraper for the really stubborn spots. Always check your manual for any special instructions from the maker. The whole job takes about half an hour, and most of that is waiting for the cleaner to work.
youNeed: White vinegar in a spray bottle
youNeedNarration: Here's what you need. Baking soda and white vinegar. A cooktop cleaner cream, made for glass or ceramic. A flat razor scraper, which is sold for cooktops, and a couple of clean microfiber cloths. And a damp towel. Don't use steel wool, scouring pads, bleach or abrasive powders, because they can scratch or stain the glass. Everything here is inexpensive and easy to find.
heroImagePrompt: A shiny black glass electric cooktop in a modern kitchen reflecting the light, with a microfiber cloth beside it, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Switch off and let it cool
steps.narration: Step one. Make sure all burners are off, and wait until the stovetop is completely cool. Many cooktops have a hot-surface light that stays on until the glass is safe to touch. Cleaning a hot surface can burn you, and cold cleaner on hot glass can leave streaks, or even crack the surface in extreme cases. Take any pans, pot holders and utensils off the top. This is also a good time to open a window and tie back long hair. Never rush this stage, because a few extra minutes of waiting makes the whole job much safer and easier.
steps.tip: Wait for the hot-surface light to go off
steps.imagePrompt: An empty cool glass electric cooktop with all pans removed, kitchen background, soft daylight, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Wipe off the loose debris
steps.narration: Step two. Start with a dry or slightly damp microfiber cloth, and wipe away crumbs, dust and any loose food. Don't push the debris around with pressure, because a hard crumb dragged across the glass can scratch it. Lift it, or sweep it into your hand. Removing this loose layer first means your cleaner can focus on the stuck-on stains. Check around the edges and the burner rings, where food tends to hide. If your stove has a control lock, activate it, so nobody switches on a burner by accident while you clean.
steps.imagePrompt: A hand wiping crumbs off a black glass cooktop with a folded microfiber cloth, bright kitchen light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Make a baking soda paste
steps.narration: Step three. Sprinkle a generous layer of baking soda over the dirty areas, then spray it with white vinegar, or hot water, until it fizzes and forms a loose paste. Baking soda is a very mild abrasive, so it won't hurt the glass, while the fizzing helps loosen residue. Soak a clean towel in hot water, wring it out and lay it over the area for fifteen to twenty minutes. The warm moisture softens burnt-on food, so you won't need force later. If the towel cools down, replace it with a fresh hot one. The longer the stain stays damp and warm, the easier it comes off.
steps.tip: Warm damp towel loosens burnt spots
steps.mistake: Using powdered cleaners with gritty particles
steps.imagePrompt: Baking soda and white vinegar foaming on a glass cooktop surface, overhead view, kitchen light, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Wipe it clean
steps.narration: Step four. Remove the towel and use a microfiber cloth or a soft sponge to wipe the paste away in gentle circles. Rinse your cloth often in warm water so you don't spread dirt around. For general grime, you will see the residue lifting easily now. Wipe the whole surface down with a clean damp cloth to remove all the baking soda. If any burnt patches remain, move on to the next step instead of scrubbing harder. Resist the urge to press hard. If a spot refuses to move, the right answer is more time, not more force.
steps.mistake: Scrubbing harder instead of soaking longer
steps.imagePrompt: A soft sponge wiping white baking soda paste off a black glass cooktop in circles, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Scrape stubborn spots safely
steps.narration: Step five. For burnt-on spots, apply a few drops of cooktop cleaner to the spot, and let it sit for a few minutes. Hold a razor scraper at a shallow angle, about thirty to forty-five degrees, and push it gently across the spot with light, even pressure, always keeping the blade flat on the glass. Never scrape with the corner, and never use a worn or damaged blade. Wipe off the residue as you go. Wear a glove, and keep your fingers behind the blade. Always check that the scraper is designed for glass cooktops, and replace the blade when it gets dull or chipped.
steps.tip: Keep the blade low and flat
steps.imagePrompt: A flat razor scraper held at a shallow angle on a glass cooktop removing a burnt spot, close-up, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Polish with cooktop cleaner
steps.narration: Step six. Now put a small amount of cooktop cleaner cream on the glass, and rub it over the whole surface with a clean cloth or paper towel. This cream cleans lightly, removes the film left by earlier cleaning, and leaves a protective layer. Let it dry to a light haze if the directions say so, and then buff it off with a dry microfiber cloth, using circular motions. You should see a clear, streak-free shine. A thin coat is enough. Polish in the direction of the light, and you will spot any streaks instantly. A dry cloth finishes the job.
steps.imagePrompt: A hand buffing a gleaming black glass cooktop with a dry microfiber cloth, reflections of a window, photorealistic, no text

steps.title: Prevent burnt-on messes
steps.narration: Step seven. A few habits will make future cleaning faster. Wipe up spills as soon as the surface is cool. Take extra care with sugary spills, which can pit the glass if left to harden, and follow the manufacturer's advice. Use flat-bottomed cookware that matches the burner size, lift pans instead of sliding them, and check that the bottom is clean and dry before use. Give your stovetop a quick wipe after cooking, and a full cleaning once a week. Following these habits, your weekly cleaning will take only five minutes. Easy, and your glass will last for years.
steps.mistake: Sliding rough pan bases across the glass
steps.imagePrompt: A clean flat-bottomed pan sitting on a spotless glass cooktop in a modern kitchen, photorealistic, no text

mistakesToAvoid.narration: Here are the three mistakes that scratch glass stovetops. First, using abrasive pads, steel wool or gritty powders. They leave permanent marks. Second, cleaning while the surface is hot, which can burn you and leave streaks. And third, scraping with the corner of the blade or at a steep angle. Keep the blade flat and shallow, use light pressure, and let the cleaner and time do the work. When in doubt, check your manual. If you are ever unsure, test any new product on a small corner first.
items: Using steel wool or abrasive pads

recap.narration: Let's recap. Switch off and let it cool. Wipe off loose debris. Make a baking soda paste and warm it with a damp towel. Wipe it clean. Scrape stubborn spots safely with a flat blade. Polish with cooktop cleaner. And build the habits that prevent burnt-on messes. Seven steps, about thirty minutes, and a stovetop that gleams. Soften first, scrape last, and your glass will stay perfect.
items: Switch off and let it cool

outro: That's how you clean a glass stovetop without scratching it. If your cooktop is shining again, subscribe to WikiTube, because we publish a new how-to every single day. Tell us in the comments what the worst spill on your stove has been, and what you would like us to explain next. See you tomorrow.

metadata.title: The Best Way to Clean a Glass Stovetop Without Scratching
metadata.description:
Burnt-on spills and streaks on your glass or ceramic cooktop? In this step-by-step video you'll learn the best way to clean a glass stovetop without scratching it: let it cool, wipe loose debris, soften stains with baking soda, vinegar and a warm towel, scrape stubborn spots safely with a razor scraper, polish with cooktop cleaner, and prevent future messes. Works for electric and induction glass cooktops.

You'll need: baking soda, white vinegar in a spray bottle, a cooktop cleaner cream, a razor scraper for glass, microfiber cloths.
